# Parameters and launch files

<!-- type: tutorial · level: 2 -->

**Needs first:** [Services and actions](services-and-actions.md)

Until now the bringup's `[[component]]` rows were the whole description of
the system, and `nros` generated a launch file from them. In this chapter the
bringup gets a launch file of its own. Through it you set a parameter that the
talker reads, so it publishes twice a second with no change to its code
afterwards, and you move both nodes to another topic name with a remap. At the
end the board prints

```text
[INFO] sensor_node: [    0.097348] Publishing every 500 ms
```

and `ros2 topic list` on your host shows `/sensor/reading`, a name that
appears in no node's code.

Run every step from the root of `sensor_ws`.

## Start from the generated launch file

A bringup with no `launch/` directory gets a launch file generated from its
`[[component]]` rows on every build. Start from that file, so that adding
`launch/` changes nothing until you edit it:

```bash probe=710 track=installed variant=qemu
mkdir -p src/sensor_node_bringup/launch
cp build/nros/launch/sensor_node_bringup/launch/system.launch.xml \
   src/sensor_node_bringup/launch/system.launch.xml
cat src/sensor_node_bringup/launch/system.launch.xml
```

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!-- Generated by nros from this bringup's system.toml [[component]] rows.
     Add launch/system.launch.xml to the bringup to replace it. -->
<launch>
  <node pkg="sensor_node" exec="sensor_node" name="sensor_node"/>
  <node pkg="monitor_node" exec="monitor_node" name="monitor_node"/>
  <node pkg="server_node" exec="server_node" name="server_node"/>
  <node pkg="client_node" exec="client_node" name="client_node"/>
  <node pkg="action_server_node" exec="action_server_node" name="action_server_node"/>
  <node pkg="action_client_node" exec="action_client_node" name="action_client_node"/>
</launch>
```

From now on `launch/system.launch.xml` is used instead of the generated one.
Deleting the `launch/` directory goes back to generation, and the
`[[component]]` rows stay the list of packages the bringup runs. The file is the
[ROS 2 launch XML format](https://docs.ros.org/en/humble/How-To-Guides/Launch-file-different-formats.html),
read with the same parser, so a launch file from another ROS 2 project pastes
in. Keep each `<node>`'s `pkg` and `exec` as the generated file wrote them:
they name the package and the class it registers.

## Read a parameter in the talker

A parameter is a value a launch file gives a node. Make the talker's period
one: read `period_ms` when the node starts, and keep 1,000 ms when the
launch file sets none.

<!-- tabs -->

#### Rust

```bash probe=720 track=installed variant=qemu
cat > src/sensor_node/src/lib.rs <<'EOF'
//! `sensor_node`: publishes a `tutorial_msgs/Reading` on `/reading` once a second.

#![no_std]

use nros::{
    Callback, CallbackCtx, Component, DeclarativeNode, ExecutableNode, NodeContext, NodeOptions,
    NodeResult, TimerDuration,
};
use nros_log::{Logger, log_info};
use tutorial_msgs::msg::Reading;

static LOGGER: Logger = Logger::new("sensor_node");

pub struct Talker;

impl Component for Talker {
    const NAME: &'static str = "sensor_node";
    const ENTITY_BOUNDS: nros::EntityBounds = nros::EntityBounds::exact(1, 0, 0, 0, 0);

    fn register(ctx: &mut NodeContext<'_>) -> NodeResult<()> {
        nros_log::register_logger(&LOGGER);
        // The launch file's `<param name="period_ms" .../>`, baked in at build
        // time; 1000 ms when the launch file sets none.
        let period_ms: u64 = ctx
            .param("period_ms")
            .and_then(|v| v.parse().ok())
            .unwrap_or(1000);
        let mut node = ctx.create_node(NodeOptions::new("sensor_node"))?;
        let pub_reading = node.create_publisher_for_topic::<Reading>("/reading")?;
        let _timer =
            node.create_timer_for_callback_name("on_tick", TimerDuration::from_millis(period_ms))?;
        log_info!(&LOGGER, "Publishing every {} ms", period_ms);
        node.callback_for_name("on_tick")
            .publishes_entity(&pub_reading)?;
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl ExecutableNode for Talker {
    /// The sequence number of the last reading published.
    type State = i32;
    const HAS_TICK: bool = false;

    fn init() -> Self::State {
        0
    }

    fn on_callback(state: &mut Self::State, callback: Callback<'_>, ctx: &mut CallbackCtx<'_>) {
        if callback.as_str() == "on_tick" {
            *state = state.wrapping_add(1);
            let msg = Reading {
                sequence: *state,
                temperature_mc: 21_000 + (*state % 10) * 100,
            };
            let _ = ctx.publish_to_topic::<Reading, 32>("/reading", &msg);
            log_info!(&LOGGER, "Publishing: reading {} ({} mC)", msg.sequence, msg.temperature_mc);
        }
    }
}

nros::node!(Talker);
EOF
```

`ctx.param("period_ms")` returns the value the launch file gives, as text,
or `None`. The value is baked into the image when it is built, so reading it
costs no lookup at run time and needs no parameter store.

#### C

```bash probe=720 track=installed variant=qemu
cat > src/sensor_node/src/Talker.c <<'EOF'
// sensor_node: publishes a tutorial_msgs/Reading on /reading once a second.
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

#include <rcl/rcl.h>
#include <rclc/executor.h>
#include <rclc/rclc.h>

#include <rclc_parameter/rclc_parameter.h>

#include <tutorial_msgs/tutorial_msgs.h>

typedef struct {
    rcl_publisher_t pub;
    rcl_timer_t timer;
    rclc_parameter_server_t params;
    int32_t count;
} talker_t;

static void on_tick(rcl_timer_t* timer, int64_t last_call_time) {
    talker_t* self = RCLC_CONTAINER_OF(timer, talker_t, timer);
    (void)last_call_time;
    self->count++;
    tutorial_msgs__msg__Reading msg;
    memset(&msg, 0, sizeof msg);
    msg.sequence = self->count;
    msg.temperature_mc = 21000 + (self->count % 10) * 100;
    if (rcl_publish(&self->pub, &msg, NULL) == RCL_RET_OK) {
        printf("Publishing: reading %d (%d mC)\n", (int)msg.sequence, (int)msg.temperature_mc);
    }
}

static rcl_ret_t talker_configure(rcl_node_t* node, rclc_executor_t* executor, talker_t* self) {
    setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IOLBF, 0);
    self->count = 0;
    // The launch file's <param name="period_ms" .../>; 1000 ms when it sets none.
    rcl_ret_t rc = rclc_parameter_server_init_default(&self->params, node);
    if (rc != RCL_RET_OK) {
        return rc;
    }
    int64_t period_ms = 1000;
    (void)rclc_parameter_get_int(&self->params, "period_ms", &period_ms);
    printf("Publishing every %d ms\n", (int)period_ms);
    self->pub = rcl_get_zero_initialized_publisher();
    rc = rclc_publisher_init_default(
        &self->pub, node, ROSIDL_GET_MSG_TYPE_SUPPORT(tutorial_msgs, msg, Reading), "/reading");
    if (rc != RCL_RET_OK) {
        return rc;
    }
    self->timer = rcl_get_zero_initialized_timer();
    rc = rclc_timer_init_default(&self->timer, NULL, (uint64_t)period_ms * 1000000ULL, on_tick);
    if (rc != RCL_RET_OK) {
        return rc;
    }
    return rclc_executor_add_timer(executor, &self->timer);
}

RCLC_C_COMPONENT(talker_t, talker_configure)
EOF
```

The C node reads parameters through rclc's parameter server, which needs the
image's parameter services:

```bash probe=725 track=installed variant=qemu
sed -i 's#^domain_id = 0#domain_id = 0\nfeatures = ["param_services"]#' src/sensor_node_bringup/system.toml
```

#### C++

```bash probe=720 track=installed variant=qemu
cat > src/sensor_node/src/Talker.cpp <<'EOF'
#include "sensor_node/Talker.hpp"

#include <cstdio>

namespace sensor_node {

void Talker::on_tick() {
    ++count_;
    ::tutorial_msgs::msg::Reading msg;
    msg.sequence = count_;
    msg.temperature_mc = 21000 + (count_ % 10) * 100;
    if (pub_.publish(msg).ok()) {
        std::printf("Publishing: reading %d (%d mC)\n", static_cast<int>(msg.sequence),
                    static_cast<int>(msg.temperature_mc));
    }
}

::rclcpp::Result Talker::configure(::rclcpp::Node& node) {
    ::setvbuf(stdout, nullptr, _IOLBF, 0);
    ::rclcpp::Result r = node.create_publisher(pub_, "/reading");
    if (!r.ok()) return r;
    // The launch file's <param name="period_ms" .../>; 1000 ms when it sets none.
    int64_t period_ms = 1000;
    (void)node.get_parameter<int64_t>("period_ms", period_ms);
    std::printf("Publishing every %d ms\n", static_cast<int>(period_ms));
    return node.create_wall_timer<Talker, &Talker::on_tick>(timer_, static_cast<uint32_t>(period_ms),
                                                            this);
}

} // namespace sensor_node
EOF
```

`node.get_parameter` reads from the image's parameter store, which a
`params` feature adds:

```bash probe=725 track=installed variant=qemu
sed -i 's#^domain_id = 0#domain_id = 0\nfeatures = ["params"]#' src/sensor_node_bringup/system.toml
```

<!-- /tabs -->

## Set it in the launch file

Now give the talker a period, and move the reading topic to a name of your
choosing. Replace the launch file:

```bash probe=730 track=installed variant=qemu
cat > src/sensor_node_bringup/launch/system.launch.xml <<'EOF'
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<launch>
  <arg name="topic" default="/sensor/reading"/>

  <node pkg="sensor_node" exec="sensor_node" name="sensor_node">
    <param name="period_ms" value="500"/>
    <remap from="/reading" to="$(var topic)"/>
  </node>
  <node pkg="monitor_node" exec="monitor_node" name="monitor_node">
    <remap from="/reading" to="$(var topic)"/>
  </node>
  <node pkg="server_node" exec="server_node" name="server_node"/>
  <node pkg="client_node" exec="client_node" name="client_node"/>
  <node pkg="action_server_node" exec="action_server_node" name="action_server_node"/>
  <node pkg="action_client_node" exec="action_client_node" name="action_client_node"/>
</launch>
EOF
```

Three things changed:

- **`<arg name="topic" default="/sensor/reading"/>`** declares a launch
  argument with a default. `$(var topic)` expands it anywhere below.
- **`<param name="period_ms" value="500"/>`** inside the talker's `<node>`
  sets the parameter the code reads.
- **`<remap from="/reading" to="$(var topic)"/>`** inside both nodes renames
  the topic they create as `/reading`, so both now publish and subscribe on
  `/sensor/reading`. Remap both or neither: a remap applies to the node it is
  in, and two nodes on different names do not hear each other.

## Run it

```bash probe=740 probe-run=900 track=installed variant=qemu
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
nros run --expect 'I heard: reading 4'
```

```text probe-expect=740 variant=qemu
Publishing every 500 ms
I heard: reading 4
```

A Rust project's console, trimmed to the talker and listener:

```text
[INFO] sensor_node: [    0.097348] Publishing every 500 ms
[INFO] sensor_node: [    0.589368] Publishing: reading 1 (21100 mC)
[INFO] monitor_node: [    0.589487] I heard: reading 1 (21100 mC)
[INFO] sensor_node: [    1.089107] Publishing: reading 2 (21200 mC)
[INFO] monitor_node: [    1.089228] I heard: reading 2 (21200 mC)
[INFO] sensor_node: [    1.589211] Publishing: reading 3 (21300 mC)
[INFO] monitor_node: [    1.589331] I heard: reading 3 (21300 mC)
[INFO] sensor_node: [    2.089854] Publishing: reading 4 (21400 mC)
[INFO] monitor_node: [    2.089975] I heard: reading 4 (21400 mC)
```

Readings now arrive every half second. Change `value="500"` to another
period and run again: only the image rebuilds, and the talker's package
does not change.

The same mechanism serves a second board or a second deployment of the same
board. Two launch files in one bringup, each with its own parameters and
remaps, can run the same node packages as two different systems; chapter 9
gives the project a second image, and an image can name the launch file it
builds. A node package that reads its configuration from parameters, rather
than from constants in its code, is a node package you never fork.

## See the new name in ROS 2

Start the board in one terminal:

```bash probe=750 probe-run=600 probe-keep track=installed variant=qemu
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
nros run
```

```text probe-expect=750 variant=qemu
I heard: reading 2
```

In a second terminal, list the topics and the nodes the router knows:

```bash probe=760 track=installed variant=qemu
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_zenoh_cpp
ros2 topic list
ros2 node list
```

```text
/parameter_events
/rosout
/sensor/reading
/action_client_node
/action_server_node
/client_node
/monitor_node
/sensor_node
/server_node
```

`/sensor/reading` is the remapped topic, and the six nodes of the image are
six nodes on the ROS 2 graph. Press Ctrl-C in the first terminal when you
are done.

Compare this with what ROS 2 shows for nodes on your own machine: the same
two commands, the same names. The board's launch file decided those names
when it was built, and the graph sees the result. Nothing on the ROS 2 side
can tell that the remap happened at build time rather than at launch.

## Parameters from a file

For more than a few values, a node loads a standard ROS 2 parameter file,
named relative to the launch file:

```yaml
# launch/sensor.param.yaml
/**:                      # every node
  ros__parameters:
    use_sim_time: false
sensor_node:              # this node only
  ros__parameters:
    period_ms: 250
```

```xml
<node pkg="sensor_node" exec="sensor_node" name="sensor_node">
  <param from="sensor.param.yaml"/>
  <param name="period_ms" value="500"/>   <!-- wins over the file -->
</node>
```

The file is the same YAML a ROS 2 node loads with `--params-file`, so a
parameter file written for the same node on a ROS 2 machine works here
unchanged, and the build reads it as it reads the launch file: once, when the
image is built.

Precedence is ROS 2's: the `/**` block, then the node's own block (keyed
`sensor_node`, `/ns/sensor_node` or `/**/sensor_node`), then an inline
`<param name= value=>`. A `from=` naming a missing file is a build error.

What the image does with parameters at run time is a capability you declare
in `[system] features`:

| Declared | Parameter store (`get_parameter`, launch values) | `ros2 param` services |
| --- | --- | --- |
| nothing | Rust's `ctx.param` reads the baked value | none |
| `params` | yes | none |
| `param_services` | yes | six per node: `get`, `set`, `list`, `describe`, and two more |

`params` suits a small board whose nodes only read their configuration: each
of the six services costs memory per node. What it gives up is
`ros2 param get`, `set`, `list`, `describe` and `dump`, and the
`use_sim_time` switch.

## Read once, or read live

The talker reads `period_ms` once, in `register` or `configure`, and builds
its timer from it. That is the right shape for a value that sizes or shapes
the node: a period, a buffer length, a frame name. It is also why the launch
file is the place to set it: the value is decided when the image is built,
and every boot of the image starts with it.

A value the node should follow while it runs is read in the callback
instead, from the parameter store, on every call. With `param_services`
declared, `ros2 param set /sensor_node <name> <value>` from a ROS 2 shell
changes that live value on the board. It changes nothing a node read once:
setting `period_ms` that way would leave the timer at the period it was built
with. A value set at run time is also volatile. The next boot starts from the
launch file again, because the board has nowhere to store the change.

## If it doesn't work

- **The talker prints `Publishing every 1000 ms`:** the parameter did not
  reach it. Check that the `<param>` is inside the talker's own `<node>`, and
  that its `name` is exactly the one the code reads.
- **The listener stops hearing readings:** only one of the two nodes is
  remapped. Remap both, or neither.
- **A C build stops with `#error "<rclc_parameter/rclc_parameter.h> needs the
  param_services capability"`:** the bringup's `[system]` has no
  `features = ["param_services"]`. Add it, as the C step above does.
- **The build names a package that does not exist:** a `<node>`'s `pkg`
  names no package in the workspace. `nros check --workspace .` lists every
  such mistake before a build.

## The launch file, briefly

| Tag | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `<arg name="…" default="…"/>` | declare a launch argument |
| `<node pkg="…" exec="…" name="…"/>` | start a node |
| `<param name="…" value="…"/>` | set one parameter (inside `<node>`) |
| `<param from="….yaml"/>` | load a ROS 2 parameter file (inside `<node>`) |
| `<remap from="…" to="…"/>` | rename a topic or service (inside `<node>`) |
| `<group ns="…">` | put a group of nodes in a namespace |
| `<include file="…"/>` | include another launch file |

Substitutions: `$(var <arg>)` expands a launch argument, `$(find <pkg>)` a
package's path, and `$(env <name>)` an environment variable.

## What just happened

The bringup's launch file became **the system's description**: which nodes
run, under which names, on which topics, with which parameters. The node
packages say what a node can do; the launch file says what this system does
with them.

Where ROS 2 reads a launch file when you run `ros2 launch`, nano-ros reads it
when it builds the image. There is no `ros2 launch` step and no launch
process on the board. The build resolves the file, arguments, remaps,
parameter files and all, into a fixed system: the nodes to construct, the
names to give them, and the parameter values to bake in. The image starts
exactly that system, every time, on a board that has no file system to read a
launch file from. Editing the launch file or a parameter file rebuilds the
image, and nothing in `src/sensor_node/` changes.

The same resolved system is what the next chapter builds on. Because the
build knows, before it compiles anything, every node the image will run and
every topic, service and action they use, it can size the image's memory for
exactly that system, if you tell it what the nodes create.

## Design background

Resolving the launch file at build time, with the ROS 2 launch parser, follows
[RFC-0121](https://github.com/NEWSLabNTU/nano-ros/blob/main/docs/design/0121-workspace-first-project-layout.md)
D2 and D3.
